To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
health-related quality of life is poor in dialysis patients and that it is related to a wide range of patient, treatment, and center characteristics.

the DOPPS is a large, international, longitudinal study designed to evaluate and improve the quality of care and outcomes for patients with ESRD.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the health-related quality of life of hemodialysis patients.
the quality of life (QOL) of patients with end stage renal disease who are receiving dialysis treatment.
the quality of life of patients undergoing dialysis treatment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DOPPS study has shown that the quality of life in patients on dialysis is poor.

the DOPPS data indicate that the use of the HEMO study dose prescription is associated with a significant reduction in all-cause mortality, but that the use of higher doses (e.g., 1.4-1.5 g/kg per week) is not associated with any additional reduction in mortality.
the quality of life of patients on dialysis is generally lower than that of the general population.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DOPPS data have been instrumental in helping us to understand the relationship between dialysis practice patterns, patient outcomes and costs.

we have demonstrated that health-related quality of life can be reliably measured and is a meaningful outcome for ESRD patients, and is associated with mortality, hospitalization, and treatment choice.
our research has been able to show that there is no difference between the health-related quality of life of patients on hemodialysis and patients on peritoneal dialysis.

we have a lot of data on the health-related quality of life of dialysis patients.
